issue.title: Web grounding returns off-topic results
issue.symptom: Live 2026-11-03, ground_query: 'capital of Kazakhstan' led with a Mongolia page, 'Who painted The Night Watch?' with Dover Beach, 'boiling point of tungsten' with an ethanol calculator, 'How do your dreams work?' with data-streaming docs. She reads these as candidate context, and answers were still mostly right from weights. Labelled honestly now, but no relevance check exists.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-common/tests/test_lookup_memory.py
"""0vuz: lookup memory keeps what GAIA looked up, verbatim and with
provenance, recalls it for later questions, and tracks when to look again."""

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from gaia_common.utils.lookup_memory import (
    ARCHIVE_UNUSED_DAYS, PIN_AFTER_CONFIRMATIONS, STABLE_DAYS, VOLATILE_DAYS, LookupMemory,
    assess_answer, content_terms, is_volatile, question_match)

T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 27, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

LADY = {
    "title": "Lady of the Lake - Wikipedia",
    "url": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_of_the_Lake",
    "snippet": "The Lady of the Lake gives King Arthur the sword Excalibur and later "
               "receives it back when Bedivere throws it into the lake.",
    "domain": "en.wikipedia.org",
    "trust_tier": "trusted",
}
ONIMUSHA = {
    "title": "Onimusha: Way of the Sword",
    "url": "https://example.com/onimusha",
    "snippet": "Onimusha: Way of the Sword is an action game set in Edo-period Kyoto with demons.",
    "domain": "example.com",
}


def _crowded_memory(tmp_path):
    mem = LookupMemory(tmp_path)
    for i in range(210):
        mem.remember(f"q{i}", [{"url": f"https://s{i}.org", "title": f"Page {i}",
                                "snippet": f"The speed of the weather front number {i} in the city today."}])
    return mem


def test_common_words_alone_are_not_a_match_in_a_full_memory(tmp_path):
    mem = _crowded_memory(tmp_path)
    assert mem.recall("What is the speed of light?") == []


def test_the_rare_word_is_what_counts(tmp_path):
    mem = _crowded_memory(tmp_path)
    mem.remember("x", [{"url": "https://l.org", "title": "Light", "snippet": "The speed of light is 299,792 km per second."}])
    assert [h["title"] for h in mem.recall("What is the speed of light?")] == ["Light"]


def test_a_memory_confirmed_for_the_question_survives(tmp_path):
    mem = _crowded_memory(tmp_path)
    rid = mem.remember("x", [{"url": "https://w.org", "title": "Weather", "snippet": "The speed of the wind is high in the city."}])[0]
    assert mem.recall("What is the speed of light?") == []
    rec = mem._load(mem._find(rid))
    rec["confirmed_queries"] = ["What is the speed of light?"]
    mem._save(rec)
    assert mem.recall("What is the speed of light?")
